disease_label_per_paper: Stevens-Johnson syndrome-toxic epidermal necrolysis overlap in a patient taking quetiapine and famotidine
presentation_summary: 82-year-old Taiwanese woman with hypertension, chronic kidney disease, severe anemia, gouty arthropathy, dementia, years of bedbound status, and hospice home care was admitted for decreased urine output, generalized edema, multiple skin blisters, and bedsores.

One and a half months before admission, methoxy polyethylene glycol-epoetin beta, ferrous citrate, sodium bicarbonate, famotidine, quetiapine, and tramadol/acetaminophen had been added to chronic amlodipine, acetaminophen, and folic acid.
On admission she was afebrile to hypothermic at 35.9 C, HR 76/min, RR 20/min, and BP 116/59 mmHg; she was cachectic and malnourished, and enteral nutrition produced tarry stool.

Dermatology evaluation on hospital day 3 showed multiple ruptured bullae with shallow erosions on face, trunk, and limbs affecting 20% TBSA, positive Nikolsky sign, and oral, genital, and ocular mucosal involvement.
Admission labs showed hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL, sodium 120 mmol/L, BUN 50 mg/dL, creatinine 4.03 mg/dL, WBC 9.54 x10^9/L, neutrophils 92%, lymphocytes 1%, and eosinophils 7%.

clinical_course.event: New medications added during the previous 1.5 months, including famotidine and quetiapine.
Admission for oliguria, generalized edema, multiple skin blisters, and bedsores; no fever, significant renal dysfunction and hyponatremia.
Dermatology evaluation showed 20% TBSA erosive bullous disease with positive Nikolsky sign and oral, genital, and ocular mucosal involvement; methylprednisolone started.
New green discharge from skin abrasions; pus culture later grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa, group G beta-hemolytic Streptococcus, Proteus mirabilis, and Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron.
Skin lesions improved after 3 days of methylprednisolone; lesions recurred after taper to 40 mg every 12 hours.
Hypothermia and hypotension developed; fluid resuscitation and vasopressors were suggested but declined by family; patient died.
